extraction.name: TextVQA
extraction.description: A dataset containing 45,336 questions on 28,408 images that require reading and reasoning about text in images to answer. Images are from the Open Images dataset from categories that tend to contain text (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard). Each question-image pair has 10 ground truth answers provided by humans.
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The TextVQA dataset contains 45,336 questions asked by sighted humans on 28,408 images from the Open Images dataset from categories that tend to contain text (e.g., 'billboard', 'traffic sign', 'whiteboard'). Questions require reading and reasoning about text in the image. Each question-image pair has 10 ground truth answers provided by humans.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from the Open Images dataset from categories that tend to contain text such as 'billboard', 'traffic sign', and 'whiteboard'
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were asked by sighted humans on images from Open Images dataset. Each question-image pair has 10 ground truth answers provided by humans.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 10 ground truth answers per question-image pair
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OCR model for text detection and recognition in images
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The model can only produce one of the OCR tokens as the predicted answer when choosing to copy. 8.9% of the TextVQA questions can only be answered by combining multiple OCR tokens, which is left as future work.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and models address an important problem for visually impaired users, as studies show that up to 21% of questions asked by visually impaired users on images of their surroundings involve reading and reasoning about text captured in images.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training and benchmarking VQA models that can read text in images and answer questions by reasoning over the text and other visual content. Models that do well on this dataset will need to parse the image and question, read text in the image, identify relevant text, and recognize whether detected text can directly be the answer or if additional reasoning is required.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Question words are embedded with pre-trained GloVe embeddings and encoded with LSTM. Visual features are extracted as spatial features from grid-based convolutions and bounding box proposals. Grid-based features are obtained by average pooling 2048D features from res-5c block of pre-trained ResNet-152. Region-based features are extracted from fc6 layer of Faster-RCNN. OCR tokens are embedded with pre-trained word embeddings.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: To add the capability of reading text from an image, we rely on an OCR model which is not jointly trained with our system. We assume that the OCR model can read and return word tokens from an image, e.g. [6, 41]. The OCR model extracts M words s=s1; s2; :::; sM from the image

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Note that if the model chooses to copy, it can only produce one of the OCR tokens as the predicted answer. 8.9% of the TextVQA questions can only be answered by combining multiple OCR tokens; we leave this as future work.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: the VizWiz study [5] found that up to 21% of these questions involve reading and reasoning about the text captured in the images of a user's surroundings – 'what temperature is my oven set to?' ,'what denomination is this bill?'

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Models that do well on this dataset will not only need to parse the image and the question as in traditional VQA, but also read the text in the image, identify which of the text might be relevant to the question, and recognize whether a subset of the detected text can directly be the answer (e.g., in the case of 'what temperature is my oven set to?') or additional reasoning is required on the detected text to answer the question (e.g., 'which team is winning?').

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: we first embed the question words w1; w2; : : : ; w L of the question q with a pre-trained embedding function ( e.g. GloVe [36]) and then encode the resultant word embeddings iteratively with a recurrent network ( e.g. LSTM [15]) to produce a question embedding fQ(q). For images, the visual features are represented as spatial features, either in the form of grid-based convolutions and/or features extracted from the bounding box proposals... The grid based features are obtained by average pooling 2048 D features from the res-5c block of a pre-trained ResNet-152 [14]. The region based features are extracted from the fc6 layer of an improved Faster-RCNN model
